Subject: Pricing & latency tradeoffs — follow-up from today's demo

Hi Alex — great to meet you today. Thanks for taking the time to walk through FintechAI's use cases. Quick recap and requested next steps so we're all aligned:

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use case: real-time chat assistant for customer support and in-product guidance (low latency required for good UX).
- Secondary use case: nightly/async summarization and batch enrichment for analytics (can tolerate higher latency).
- Key constraints: target budget range, and P95 latency SLO for chat.

What we need from you to give a concrete recommendation:
1) Token volume breakdown (chat vs async) — rough monthly numbers are fine.
2) Target budget or target $/1M tokens you're aiming for.
3) Desired latency SLO (P50/P95) for the chat flow.

Ballpark from our end (we'll refine once you share volumes):
- Hosted (Standard tier): fast to start, no commit, expected unit cost ~ $30–$40 per 1M tokens for general-purpose models at interactive SLOs (P95 300–500ms).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): recommended if you want to hit < $25 per 1M tokens at scale with predictable throughput and tighter latency targets — depends on commit level and model choice.
- Hybrid: stream chat on hosted or dedicated small pool for low-latency and batch the async work with larger batching windows to reduce unit cost on the same model family.

We've attached a template (token_volume_breakdown.xlsx) you can fill in with expected monthly volumes and percent real-time vs batch — that will let us provide a tailored cost table (by tier, batching config, and streaming/continuous-inference options).

Next steps: if you can send the rough volumes and target $/1M tokens today or tomorrow, Vivek and I will put together a short cost tradeoff table showing: expected monthly cost, recommended tier (Hosted vs Dedicated), and a latency/cost sensitivity analysis (batch sizes, streaming on/off).

Thanks \u2014

Alex — super helpful, thanks for the quick breakdown. Based on 40M tokens/month (28M real-time / 12M batch) and your ~$20/1M target, here are ballpark options. These are intentionally simplified — Vivek will add technical nuance on batching and SLO impact in the next note.

Option A — Hosted Standard (no commit):
- Unit price assumption: ~ $35 per 1M tokens at interactive SLOs (P95 300–500ms), so ~ $1,400/month for 40M tokens.
- Pros: fastest to start, no contract.
- Cons: higher per-token cost — unlikely to hit $20/1M at this scale without model concessions.

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit):
- Example commit level to get near $20/1M: medium reserved pool with steady utilization. Estimated unit cost: ~$18–22 per 1M tokens depending on model and quantization (at 70–80% amortized utilization).
- For 40M tokens at $20/1M => ~$800/month.
- Pros: predictable cost, better tail latency control, and higher throughput for batching.
- Cons: requires commit and a short provisioning lead time for certain GPU types.

Option C — Hybrid (Recommended):
- Keep a small dedicated/hosted pool for chat (size tuned to peak concurrency) to meet P95 <= 300ms, and route async summarization through larger batch workers (can be scheduled to run off-peak or on cheaper GPU variants).
- With batching the 12M async tokens could see 25–40% unit-cost reduction vs interactive pricing depending on batching window and model choice — this helps pull the blended $/1M closer to your $20 target.

Quick math (blended example):
- Chat (28M) on dedicated at $22/1M = $616
- Async (12M) batched at effective $12/1M = $144
- Blended total = $760 (~$19/1M effective)

Hi Alex / Marissa — quick technical follow-up on the tradeoffs mentioned above. Tl;dr: hybrid + small dedicated pool for chat + aggressive batching for async gets you closest to $20/1M while preserving P95 targets. Details below.

1) Chat (real-time) recommendations:
- Streaming RPCs with incremental token flush will reduce perceived latency for users even if model inference takes slightly longer. Use token-level streaming for user-facing chat.
- Aim for a dedicated pool sized to handle peak concurrency with continuous batching turned on but with low max batch delay (5–15ms) to keep tail latency tight.
- Model pick: pick a lower-latency variant or a quantized profile if response quality is acceptable — this often moves unit economics 15–30% depending on model.

2) Async (summaries & enrichments):
- Batch window 200–800ms (or schedule overnight large batches) to maximize throughput. Higher batch sizes amortize kernel/kernel-init overhead and dramatically reduce per-token cost.
- If you can tolerate a few-second latency, push batch sizes higher and use cheaper model variants for enrichment tasks.

3) Caching & KV reuse:
- For chat flows with repeated prompts or system prompts, prefix caching (KV cache) reduces compute and lowers cost. Ensure session affinity for best cache hit rates.

4) Sizing and cost guidance (very rough):
- With 28M chat tokens and low-latency dedicated pool + 12M batched tokens, the blended $/1M in Marissa's example (~$19/1M effective) is achievable with ~70–80% sustained utilization of the dedicated pool and conservative batching for async.

Open questions for your infra team on the follow-up call:
- Peak concurrency numbers (users/sec) and average message length (tokens per message).
- Will you require workplace isolation / VPC or are hosted endpoints acceptable?
- Any compliance/security questionnaires we should preemptively prepare for procurement?

I can put together a one-pager with concrete pool sizes and expected P95 numbers for our recommended config if you want to share concurrency and avg tokens/message.

—Vivek
